name: Uzziel
overview: Uzziel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as the son of Kohath. His role and significance are primarily established through his lineage within the Levitical family, which held a special place in Israel's religious structure. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Uzziel means 'G-d [El] is [my] strength,' reflecting a declaration of divine empowerment. This proper name, as recorded, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological affirmation.
familyAndRelationships: Uzziel is explicitly identified as the son of Kohath. Inferred from Scripture are his roles as the father of Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri. Additionally, he is an ancestor to Amminadab, Micah, and Isshiah, indicating his place within a broader Levitical genealogy.
scriptureSignificance: Uzziel's importance in the biblical narrative lies in his position within the Levitical lineage, which was foundational to the priestly and religious duties of Israel. As a son of Kohath, he contributed to the heritage that shaped the Levitical family's responsibilities. His descendants continued this legacy, underscoring the ongoing role of his line in serving the Lord and supporting the worship system established by God.
